entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 19.1.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`formatRelativeTime(at, locale?, { now?, style? })`** from `@oxy.so/bloom/locale` and the root: "3 minutes ago" / "in 2 days" in the reader's locale through a cached `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` (English words where the engine lacks it). Apps can use it in place of their own time-ago helpers.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 19.0.0
entries.content:
### Breaking

- **Remove `richColors` from toast options and `ToasterProps`.** Remove the prop from `toast.*(...)` calls and `<ToastOutlet>` configuration. The toast card, border and title remain neutral for every variant; status is conveyed by the leading disc. `richColors` no longer changes toast paint.

### Changed

- **Use compact toast geometry for every content shape.** Toasts with descriptions or actions now use the same 12px vertical padding and 28px status disc as a one-line toast. Actions without a description sit inline; actions with a description sit below the text.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.5.2
entries.content:
### Changed

- **One release rule for every pan a bottom sheet owns.** Whether a released pan closes the sheet (a downward flick over 900 px/s, or a pull past the larger of 140 px and a quarter of the screen that is not already returning upward) was written out three times in `BottomSheetBase`; it is now one function. The thresholds are the same, so a sheet closes and springs back exactly as before.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.5.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A roving group's arrows move one option per press, however late the host's focus.** A key chose the next option from the one the host last said had the focus, and the option a key chose stopped counting once its value landed, before the host's focus moved there. A host that read several ↓ in the turn that moved the focus for the first (a loaded machine, while the first one's page rendered) had each choose the row the first had chosen: eight presses in a settings rail, one move. The option chosen now stays the one the keys go on from until the host's focus lands on it (its `onFocus`), and the host's focus and blur are taken at once.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.5.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **Desktop density for grouped forms and settings.** `GroupedSection density="compact"` draws a desktop form's groups, as a Mac's System Settings does: 36-point rows (padding 10 × 6) in the body style, regular, a hairline between rows inset at the text of the row above, a 12 radius, the title in the headline style as it is written (no forced capitals) and aligned with the rows' text, and no outer margin (the page's stack spaces sections). The density comes from the new `BloomScope contentDensity` (`'comfortable' | 'compact'`, `useBloomContentDensity()`) when a section does not say; `comfortable` is unchanged.
- **`SettingsLayout density="compact"`**: 28-point rail rows in the body style and the label's colour, groups apart by space alone (no headings), a 20 content inset and compact sections in its pages.
- **`SettingsLayout search`**: a controlled search field at the top of the rail (`SettingsSearchProps`), its owner filtering the groups; Escape clears it, ↓ and Return go to the first result (chosen, its page shown, the keyboard on its row on a native host), and `labels.noResults` says when nothing matches (`search` and `noResults` in every Bloom language).
- **`SettingsLayout`'s handle** (`ref`, `SettingsLayoutHandle`: `focusSearch()`, `back()`, `forward()`) and `onHistoryChange({ canGoBack, canGoForward })`, for the owner's Edit › Find… and View › Back and Forward.
- **`useNativeRovingGroup().focusItem(value)`**: brings the keyboard into a roving group at an option, as an arrow reaching it does (a search field's ↓ into its results).

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.4.4
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A desktop `AlertDialog` is a desktop alert.** `Dialog` hands its content on wrapped in its frame scope (`DialogFrameContent`), so `hasChildren` always saw content and no dialog drawn through `Dialog` was ever an alert on a desktop: an `AlertDialog` or `confirm()` kept the 480px card instead of the 280px alert (17.42.0), and its keyboard and screen reader started on its first button, Cancel, not its default (18.4.2, 18.4.3). `hasChildren` now counts what that wrapper holds.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.4.3
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A desktop dialog with content starts in its content.** 18.4.2 gave a desktop dialog's default button the initial focus whenever no action asked for it, which is right for an alert but moved a dialog with content of its own off its content: a sheet with a list (OxyOS Settings' input methods) opened with the keyboard on Add, not on its first row. The default button now takes it only in an alert, a dialog of its declarative chrome alone; an action that asks still wins anywhere.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.4.2
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A desktop alert starts on its default button.** 17.42.0 put the default button last in a desktop alert's row, but only an action that asked for the initial focus (`initialFocus`, `defaultAction`) took it, so an alert that asked for none (a `confirm()`, OxyOS Settings' sign-out) started the keyboard and the screen reader on its first button, Cancel. On a desktop the default button now takes it when no action asks (`desktopInitialFocus`), as a Mac's alert does; one that asks still wins (`defaultAction: 'cancel'`).

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.4.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A desktop menu is as wide as its widest row on native.** 17.42.0 gave a desktop platform's menus their content's width, but each row's label kept `flex-1`, whose `flex: 1` makes Yoga's flex basis 0 whatever `flexBasis` says, so a panel sized by its content was held at its 120px floor and cut its labels (OxyOS's dock menu showed "Mostrar toda…"). On a desktop the label now grows and shrinks from its own width (`flexGrow`/`flexShrink`, no `flex`).

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.4.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`ResponsiveGrid flow="columns"`**: cells fill independent column stacks (cell 1 to column 1, cell 2 to column 2, …) instead of aligned rows, so cells of very different heights (the sections of a detail page) sit one under the other with no gap under the short ones. The column count is still chosen from the measured container (`minItemWidth`, `maxColumns`), and one column when narrow. In this mode a cell moves column when the count changes, so it remounts. `flow="rows"` (default) is exactly as before.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.3.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`AiProfileCard` is an identity on its own.** `contributions` and `cells` are optional: without `contributions` the headline (label, count-up, delta) is not drawn, without `cells` the Activity row and the heatmap are not, and the `stats` tiles were already optional. A profile that has only a person's name, handle and picture (a public account, with no activity of its own to count) is the cover, the avatar and the name row, with `actions`. A card given all of them is drawn exactly as before.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.2.2
entries.content:
### Changed

- **A table shows its sort chevron on the sorted column alone.** A sortable `TableColumn` with `sortDirection` `'none'` drew the same chevron as the sorted one (in the header's colour, which is the sorted one's too), so every sortable header looked sorted, unlike a desktop table (macOS's, Finder's list), whose headers show the indicator only where the table is sorted. An unsorted column now keeps the chevron's room, drawn transparent, so no label moves as the sort goes from column to column; `aria-sort` and the header's button are unchanged.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.2.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- Register Bloom's `web:` utility variant in the standalone Vite recipe so bounded desktop panel layers retain their grid geometry.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.2.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`SettingsPageActions`**: settings pages can put Save/Cancel actions in their header, grouped beside close, while the page retains its dirty/saving state. `SettingsModal` and `SettingsLayout` also accept `headerPresentation="floating"` for Bloom’s floating `PageHeader`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.1.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **Android composer caret survives busy and loader transitions.** A focused controlled `TextInput` could move its caret to the end when the Stop control or loader changed the pill. The native selection is restored after layout on Android, and width changes also preserve collapsed selections. Verified on a Pixel 8a through resize, busy/Stop, continued typing and rotation; evidence is in `docs/audits/issue-663/composer-input-rotation-pixel8a-2026-11-10/`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.1.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`AgentCreator sections` and `AgentCreatorSection`**: titled cards of the host's own below the details card, for what an agent *has* beyond who it is (its schedule, its inbox, what it remembers). `AgentCreatorSection title` draws the card with the details card's surface, radius and inset; its rows are `AgentCreatorField`s (or any row of the host's). They scroll with the rest of the editor. `children` stays the way to add rows to the details card itself.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 18.0.0
entries.content:
### Removed

- **The agent creator's "Avatar style" row.** `CharacterControls` offered a select of ready-made character presets above eyewear and accessory. A person editing or creating an agent builds a character from its parts (shape, eyes, colour, eyewear, accessory), and a preset there only replaced all of them at once, so the row is gone. The `avatarStyle` and `betaPreset` message keys of `AgentCreatorMessages` go with it (and from every locale). `CHARACTER_PRESETS`, `CHARACTER_TEMPLATES` and `characterTemplateChoice` stay exported for code that starts from a template.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.50.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`AiChatShell panelFloatingBelow`** (`'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' | number`, default `'xl'`): the width below which the context panel stops sitting beside the conversation and floats over it as a dialog. It was fixed at `xl`, so a narrow panel worked in beside the thing it edits (an agent editor, 380px) became a modal with the page dimmed under it on any laptop window under 1280px, though the sidebar, a 320px conversation and the panel fit from `lg`. A host whose panel is that kind sets `'lg'`; nothing changes without it.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 24.2.0
entries.content:
- **Composer loader lifecycle.** `useConversationThread` exposes `composerPhase` separately from
  `isLoading`; `AliaChatContent` passes the request phase to `AliaComposer`, which forwards it to
  Bloom's `ComposerLoader`. Direct `AliaComposer` callers may pass `loaderPhase` themselves.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.46.0
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **An avatar never draws a path with `NaN` in it.** The vector avatar's clock is added to every frame and kept for the life of the avatar, so a single frame callback without a usable timestamp (a shimmed `requestAnimationFrame`, a webview that omits it) made every later pose, and every contour and clip path drawn from it, `NaN`, and the browser rejected each one (`<path> attribute d: Expected number, "MNaN NaN…"`). The step now comes from `vectorFrameDelta`: only a finite, forward step counts, and a frame with no timestamp is read off `performance.now()`. `renderVectorFrame` draws the rest pose for a `time`, `yaw` or `pitch` that is not finite, and leaves out a part whose projection is not finite rather than writing it as path data. No frame the renderer drew from valid input changes.

entries.title: @alia-codea/cli 3.4.0
entries.content:
`codea connect` continues the CLI's own session for each Alia conversation (Claude Code
`--resume`, Codex `exec resume`), so the agent keeps its tool context between messages and no longer
gets the whole conversation re-sent. If the CLI lost the session it starts a new one on its own.
Sessions are remembered across restarts of the daemon.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.42.0
entries.content:
### Added

On a **desktop platform** (`useDesktopPlatform()`: an adapter reporting `window` or `pointer`, an OxyOS window or shell) Bloom draws a desktop's own compact chrome. Phones and the web are unchanged.

- **Desktop text styles** (`DESKTOP_TEXT_STYLES`, `DESKTOP_TYPE_SCALE`, `DESKTOP_TRACKING`, `desktopTextStyle`, `resolveTypeScale`): one style per role, 13/16 body, tracking by size; `Text` variants map onto them and titles take the sans. `TypographyScope scale` opts in or out.
- **Neutral surfaces** (`BloomThemeProvider surfaces`, `SurfaceTint`, `ExplicitAccents.surfaces`): page, surfaces, text and boundaries in greys of no hue, the default on a desktop; the accent stays the seed's.
- **Label levels** (`resolveLabelColors`, `useLabelColors`, `LABEL_ALPHA`): the ink at 1 / 0.65 / 0.42 / 0.18.
- **Compact desktop menus**: 22px rows of 13px text, 5px panel padding, radius 10/5, content width (120 floor), accent highlight, a clear shadow, the arrow pointer, shortcuts in a trailing column (`DESKTOP_MENU_GEOMETRY`, `DESKTOP_MENU_SHADOW`).
- **One desktop alert layout** for `AlertDialog`, `confirm()`/`alert()` and declarative `Dialog`: narrow, icon, bold title, buttons sized to their labels, the default accent-filled, trailing in a row and on top of a stack. New `icon` on `Dialog`, `AlertDialog` and `confirm()`.
- **Tooltip delay** of one second on a desktop, with a 500 ms warm window (`DESKTOP_TOOLTIP_DELAY`, `TOOLTIP_WARM_WINDOW`); an explicit `delay` wins.
- **The platform's material**: the `material` capability and its `Material` view (`PlatformMaterialProps`, `usePlatformMaterial()`), drawn under a floating surface's tint.

### Fixed

- The settings rail's hover is the documented 60% wash, no longer the selected fill.
- `Switch` fades disabled at the one `DISABLED_OPACITY` (0.5), not 0.4.

entries.title: @alia-codea/cli 3.3.1
entries.content:
`codea connect` lets the agent edit files in its working directory by default: read-only made Claude
Code and Codex answer "I don't have permission" to almost anything. Start it with `--read-only` to
forbid changes, and the agent then says how to lift that instead of just refusing. Run it from the
folder you want the agent to work in.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.41.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`ComposerLoader.phase`** (`idle`, `submitting`, `streaming`, `stopping`, `error`, `complete`) gives chat composers one controlled request lifecycle. Bloom owns the fade and motion; the app continues to own submission, cancellation, error and completion. `active` remains compatible during the 17.x migration. `AgentChat` maps its transport-neutral statuses and accepts `composerPhase` when an app needs explicit stopping/completion phases.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 24.1.0
entries.content:
- **A consulted agent's reply is not drawn under its line.** When Alia or an agent asks another
  agent (`consultAgent`), the thread shows "Chatted with …" and no longer the agent's answer
  beneath it: the lead already answers the person with it, and the line opens the exchange
  (`onOpenAgentChat`) to read it. A host that passes no `onOpenAgentChat` keeps the answer where it
  was, since there would be no way to reach it. Members of a group chat are never consulted
  agents: they speak as themselves. New `consultedReplies` beside `speakerChanges`.

entries.title: @alia-codea/cli 3.3.0
entries.content:
`codea connect` serves Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode to Alia as one of your agents
([ADR 0028](../../docs/adr/0028-external-agents.md)). Create a code in Alia (Settings → Connect an
external agent), paste the text it gives you into your agent, and it runs
`codea connect --code <code> --cli <claude|codex|opencode>`. The process dials Alia outbound with your
Oxy session and answers the messages Alia sends it by running the CLI you are already signed in to, in
the current directory, read-only unless started with `--write`. Run `codea connect` again to serve the
agents this machine is paired with.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 24.0.1
entries.content:
- **A conversation prefetch never retries.** `prefetchConversation` (the hover/press-in warm-up)
  now fails once and quietly. It used to retry through the query client's default policy, so a
  refusal by the API's rate limit (429) was retried twice more, spending the budget that had just
  refused it; the press that opens the conversation fetches it itself.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.40.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`MenubarItem action="about"` and `action="settings"`**: the application's own About *App* and Settings…, as a Mac's application menu has them (`PlatformMenuAction`). They are the application's items, never a focused text field's (their `onPress` or `href` and `disabled`; disabled with neither); Settings… has the standard chord `Mod+,` (⌘, on a Mac, Ctrl+, elsewhere), which runs it on every platform. Drawn in the window they stay where they are declared. With the `menu-bar` capability each is described with its `action` (`PlatformMenuItem.action`), so a platform whose bar has an application menu of its own (OxyOS's, a Mac's) shows it there, as AppKit puts Settings… in the application menu (OxyOS ADR 0021).

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.39.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A flush `plain` sidebar leaves no gap before the region beside it.** Its rows already carry their own inset, and it has no panel to space the region from, yet the shell still put the navigation gap (16 by default) between it and the panels, so the sidebar's end side kept a gutter the start side had lost. The region now starts at the sidebar's edge, on the web layout and the native engine alike (a docked sidebar keeps the frame's gutter, a card sidebar its `navigationGap`).

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 24.0.0
entries.content:
- **Breaking.** The web search switch is gone: Alia can always search the web, so
  `AliaTurnRequest.webSearch` (what `AliaRuntimeHost.turnRequest` returned) is removed. Hosts that
  returned it from `turnRequest`: delete it. The server still accepts `webSearch: false` from
  other clients on `/v1`.
- **Group chats.** A conversation of several agents (`memberAgentIds`, the `group` prop of
  `AliaChatContent`) gets its own welcome (`AliaGroupWelcome`, the members' avatars together), and
  the members' avatars fly out of it with the first message. Its members speak as themselves: no
  "chat with" line is drawn at each change of speaker.
- **Group rooms in real time.** The members of a group talk to each other past the request. The
  host gets a new optional hook, `AliaRuntimeHost.subscribeRoomEvents(conversationId, listener)`,
  fed from the `group:event` socket event; the thread draws a member typing, streams what the
  members write and stores their replies as they land. A host that does not implement it keeps
  today's behaviour (the request's own first round).
- **Agent threads read as a chat.** In a chat with an agent (or a group) the thread shows the
  conversation only: no "Worked for" line, task list or search trail, and the agent's tools do not
  open the thought panel on their own. Alia's own chat is unchanged.
- **"Chatted with …"** (before "Chat with …") is a button: it opens, read-only and without the
  composer, the conversation the agents had between themselves (what the calling agent asked and
  what the consulted agent answered), rebuilt from the loaded messages. The chat under it stays
  mounted and inert, so its scroll and draft survive.
- **Bubbles.** The person's own bubble has no react button (a reaction is a vote on a reply); the
  react, reply and more icons and the reaction pill are the chat reference's own.
- Built and tested against Bloom 17.39.0. The peer range stays `@oxy.so/bloom >=17.22.0`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.39.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`Sidebar scrollbarSide`** (`'start' | 'end'`, default `'end'`): the inline edge the sidebar's scrolling area draws its scrollbar on. A flush `plain` sidebar has its scrollbar against the neighbouring panel; `start` moves it to the sidebar's outer edge. It is logical, so `start` is the right edge in RTL. Built on the new `ScrollArea scrollbarSide` and `ScrollBar side` (and the `ScrollAreaScrollbarSide` type), which any scroller can use; vertical bars only. Web only: a native scroll indicator is the system's and stays where the platform draws it.
- **`AiChatShell sidebarScrollbarSide`**: the shell hands it to a function `sidebar` as `scrollbarSide` (it is also accepted by `ConversationSidebar` and the `AppShell` sidebar descriptor, which are `SidebarProps`).

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.38.0
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **`ComposerLoader` follows the composer's corner radius.** A `ComposerPill` is a full capsule at one line and squares off to 26 when it grows into a stack (several lines, attachments, a status tab), but the loader around it kept the capsule radius, so a grown pill had an oval container and rim light behind it. The pill now reports its radius to the loader (`ComposerLoaderRadiusContext`, `useReportComposerRadius`) and the loader paints and traces that; a `radius` passed to the loader still wins, and with no composer inside it is the capsule as before.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.37.0
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A plain sidebar is flush to the window in the web's CSS layout too.** 17.36.0 made a `plain` sidebar run flush beside a panel region, but only in the engine's inline styles; the browser lays the shell out with generated CSS (`shell-layout-css.ts`) that overrode them with its own copy of the rule, so on the web the sidebar still sat inside the frame's gutter and the region beside it added a second one. The rule is now ONE function, `plainNavFlushes`, that the engine, the CSS layout and `flushSidebarAtEveryWidth` all ask, so they cannot disagree again.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.36.0
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A `plain` sidebar is flush to the window beside any panel region**, not only beside a centred reading column. `AppShell` already ran a plain nav flush when the content was centred (`navigationAlign="content"`), since a plain nav has no panel to frame; with a panel region that is not a centred column (a chat beside its sidebar, as `AiChatShell` draws it) the nav stayed inside the frame's gutter, floating with a gap at its start, top and bottom and nothing behind it. It now takes the whole height at the window's edge, as a `docked` one does, and the panel region keeps its own gutter on its other sides. `card` is unchanged. `AiChatShell` defaults to `plain`, so a host that did not pass `sidebarSurface` gets the flush sidebar; `sidebarSurface="card"` keeps the framed panel.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.35.0
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **Agent avatars fill their box.** Every vector frame is authored on a 320×320 canvas with room for the figure to move, and the avatar drew the whole canvas: at rest the characters span about 174 of its 320 units, so a 32px avatar was a 17px character with empty space around it. The avatar (`VectorCharacterAvatar` and the static portrait) is now drawn through one shared square crop around the figures (`vector-viewbox.ts`), so they fill about 80% of their box instead of 54%, and keep their relative sizes. A frame that carries a viewBox of its own (the eyes-only preview) is unchanged.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.34.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`ComposerPanelAddMenuGroup submenu` / `icon`**: a group drawn as ONE row that opens its rows in a submenu, instead of a heading over them. For a list that can grow long (a person's skills, their connected apps) and would push the menu's few common rows out of reach.
- **`DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` and `DropdownMenuRadioItem` take `leading`**, as `DropdownMenuItem` does.

### Fixed

- **The composer's add menu rows line up.** A switch row passed its icon as a child, so the menu's row alignment saw a row with no icon and put a blank icon-wide slot in front of it: Search, Deep research and Ghost sat one icon further in than Camera, Photos and Files. The switch's icon is now the row's own `leading`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom-editor 0.8.0
entries.content:
### Added

- Native selection actions for links and formatting, with explicit link editing that preserves the active text input and IME.
- Shared Bloom Popover ownership for editor link overlays, including live caret anchoring on web.

### Compatibility

- Requires `@oxy.so/bloom` 17.24.0 or newer for the shared virtual-anchor API.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.31.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`AiChatShell sidebarSurface`** (`plain` by default): the in-flow sidebar's panel. The shell lays out its gutters by the surface it is given, so a host that wants the raised `card` panel declares it here and the shell keeps the gap around and beside it; a `card` drawn inside a shell that declared `plain` ran flush to the window edge with the wrong gaps.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.30.2
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **The morphing spinner's points are evenly spaced.** The outline's arc length was measured in unit coordinates against samples stored in viewbox units, so points bunched up and neighbouring frames no longer corresponded; transitions looked lumpy at corners. The largest gap between points was about ten times the mean and is now under one and a half.
- **The web `SpinnerIcon` is in the markup.** Its path had no `d` until the first animation frame, so server-rendered HTML and the first paint showed no loading indicator. The first frame is now in the first render and the loop keeps rewriting the same `d`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.30.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **`ChatHeader` uses its measured width** to choose compact gutters and default back-button visibility. `showBack` remains available when navigation context differs from available width.

entries.title: @alia.onl/sdk 23.1.0
entries.content:
- Reactions in the chat bubbles: Bloom's emoji bar on a message, the person's reactions as pills
  under the bubble and everyone's votes under "more". They toggle through
  `POST /v1/conversations/:id/messages/:messageId/reactions`.
- Fix: the persisted conversation list hands its dates back as `Date`s (a hydrated list held
  `updatedAt` as an ISO string and the sidebar's sort threw `updatedAt.getTime is not a function`).
- Built and tested against Bloom 17.29.0, where the spinner of every busy state (`Loading`,
  `Button`, the send button) is the Material 3 morphing loader. The peer range stays
  `@oxy.so/bloom >=17.22.0`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.30.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`AgentCreator` takes rows of the host's own**: `children` are drawn in the details card after the description, composed with the new `AgentCreatorField` (the row the editor's Name, Label and Description now use), so a host's rows match the editor's geometry, hairlines and type. Nothing changes without children.
- **`AiChatShell panelResizable`** (default `true`): `false` removes the divider beside the context panel, which then keeps `defaultPanelWidth`. For a panel with a width of its own, such as an editor.
- **`ConversationSidebar heading`**: a label over the conversation rows ("Agents"), drawn like a tree section's, for a rail that titles its list. Not drawn without rows.
- **Sidebar tree rows with a `description`** give their `leading` a taller box (`tree.avatar`: 32, 36 and 40px by size) instead of the 20px glyph box, so a contact's picture is as tall as its two lines of text. Rows without a description are unchanged.

### Fixed

- **`AiChatShell` owns the sidebar's collapse** when `sidebar` is a function `(props) => ReactNode`: the shell hands it its resolved props (`collapsed`, `onCollapsedChange`, `variant`, `mobile`...), so the sidebar's own collapse control also resizes the shell's track and gives the room to the conversation, with the shell's motion. Before, the adapter pinned the track expanded (`collapsed: false`) and ignored those props, so collapsing only moved the sidebar's contents inside a track that stayed 260px wide. A `sidebar` node behaves as before.
- **The composer's add menu is built on Bloom's `DropdownMenu`**, not rows of buttons in a panel of its own. Its action rows (Camera, Photos, Files, Canvas) were centred, because the row buttons never set how they lay their content out; the menu now has the family's row layout (left-aligned, an icon that leads, a switch's check mark at the end) and its semantics (roving focus, arrow keys). The `-add-panel` test id stays on the menu surface; a switch row is a checkbox row (`aria-checked`) with the test id `bloom-row-<id>`, replacing `bloom-row-checked-<id>`.

### Changed

- **`AgentCreator`'s `agent.handle` (17.28.0) is removed** in favour of `children` rows: a host's username (or anything else of its own) is an `AgentCreatorField` row, not a field the editor knows about.
- **`AgentCreator`'s header carries undo and redo** as icon buttons (`avatarHistory` group), and the React, Work and Restore original buttons are gone.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.29.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- **The spinner is the Material 3 morphing loader**: `SpinnerIcon`, and so every `Loading` variant, `Button` busy state and engagement-bar busy glyph, now draws a solid shape that morphs through the Material loading loop (soft burst, cookie, pentagon, pill, sunny, cookie, oval) while it rotates, instead of the eight-blade iOS spinner. entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.47.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **`createOxySocketCors` admits a WebSocket handshake from the server's own origin.** A native WebSocket client sends the socket URL's own origin when its caller gives none (React Native's Android WebSocketModule, iOS's SocketRocket, OxyOS), and `allowRequest` admitted only no `Origin` or an allow-listed one, so every native app's socket to a service outside the Oxy apex family was refused with `400` (OxyOS#477: Alia's realtime socket on OxyOS, Android and iOS). An `Origin` equal to the request's `Host` with the scheme of the first `X-Forwarded-Proto` value (else of the connection being TLS) is same-origin and admitted; scheme and port are part of the comparison. Every other origin keeps the allow-list rules, the opaque `null` still refused. The long-polling `cors` answer is unchanged: a same-origin request needs no CORS headers. New type `OxySocketHandshakeRequest`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.19.0
entries.content:
### Changed

- **On a session host that names the platform's languages, they are the app's language, and nothing waits for the account** (ADR 0058 R11, ADR 0022). R10 needed the account's languages in the snapshot, which a real account often lacks (the platform keeps them only after a profile read, and an account may have none): OxyOS's Dropsea still showed a blank window for 6 to 15 s on the owner's ThinkPad, waiting for the boot token and `GET /users/me`, then spoke the fallback rather than the system's language. Where the host's snapshot carries `preferredLanguages`, `currentLanguage` is the platform's from the first render, signed in or out, online or not, over the account's and the profile's; `isLanguageReady` and `isAccountLanguageKnown` are true at once and `OxyProvider`'s `language` bridge waits for neither the token, the profile, the guest override nor storage. A host without them keeps R10.
- **The language bridge shows the app in the commit that knows its language.** When the language is known at mount and the app's `language.onChange` applies it synchronously (an in-memory locale store), the bridge's children are in the same commit, so the app's first frame is its own content rather than an empty window; an asynchronous `onChange` is still awaited, and a later locale still waits for an earlier catalog.

### Consumers

Needs `@oxy.so/core` 7.47.0.

entries.content:

A platform that sends it receives its credential pending: it proves nothing until `POST /session/device/platform/confirm` confirms it, and is gone ten minutes after the QR's claim or the sign-in; the credential the sign-in's device proof presented is retired only by the confirmation. entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.16.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **`OxySetupFlow`: a platform's setup in the sign-in's own frame** (ADR 0064). A controlled, presentational multi-step frame: the host passes its `steps` (`OxySetupStep`: `id`, `title`, `description`, `icon`, `content`, `aside`, `initialFocus`, `primary`, `secondary`) and the `current` id, and owns what every action does. Each step is drawn in the SDK sign-in's shell (the icon or the Oxy mark, the 48/800 title, blocks 24 apart, 448 wide; with an `aside`, the split card from `md`, asking for 880), with Back leading and the secondary and primary actions trailing, quiet progress ("Step 2 of 5" and decorative dots), Bloom's `ScreenTransition` between steps (none under reduced motion), focus moved to the new step's title (or left to its content), and the change said politely ("Create a PIN, step 3 of 5"). `onMaxWidthChange` reports the width the current step asks, as `OxySurfaceFrame` does.
- **`oxySignInStep()`**: the SDK's sign-in as a step — `OxyAuthChooser`, unchanged, inside the flow's surface-width context, so the card grows to the QR split's 880 for that step and returns after. The host still learns the sign-in through `authStateStore` (`PlatformSetupAuthStateStore`); there is no second seam.
- `OxyAuthScreenHeader` takes `icon` (in place of the Oxy mark) and `titleRef`.

### Consumers

No API removed. Needs `@oxy.so/core` 7.45.0 (the announcement's words). OxyOS's login screen composes its setup with it.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.23.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **Semantic header actions.** `HeaderActions` and PageHeader action descriptors share command placement, priority and overflow behavior with dialog headers. Applications supply labels, permissions and callbacks; the shared header owns responsive presentation and accessible action state.
- **Focused chart entries.** Bar lists, line charts, surfaces, headers and stat tiles are available through `@oxy.so/bloom/chart-cards/bar-list`, `/line`, `/surface`, `/header` and `/stat-tiles`, without importing the full chart family barrel.

### Fixed

- Horizontal ScrollArea and Toolbar owners reveal the entire focused control after keyboard entry and viewport narrowing, including RTL. Resize correction runs directly after layout, preserving surrounding panel and document offsets; callback-ref cleanup is retained.
- Coarse-pointer web buttons reserve a real 44×44 CSS-pixel interactive minimum, including icon actions, links and button groups, while fine-pointer geometry remains unchanged.
- Hidden composer loaders suspend animation and preserve their measured phase on resumption. Native loader lifecycle follows its activity owner.
- IconCircle accepts canonical Bloom icon components without consumer casts. Document-panel bottom clearance stays inside its material surface.

### Validation and adoption

Shared-owner regression suites and browser interaction runners cover header overflow, actual touch hit testing, loader lifetime, panel paint and horizontal focus. Horizontal focus includes Chromium and WebKit with LTR/RTL and reduced motion; these browser results are not physical iPhone validation. Consumer adoption remains explicit: use the shared header action descriptors and ScrollArea owner, and consume the focused chart entry needed by the app. Editor selection/link-overlay migration remains separate work.

entries.title: @oxy.so/contracts 6.22.0
entries.content:
A QR redemption repeats with its key (ADR 0058 R7, 2026-11-08).

### Added

- `platformSession.ts`: `redemptionKeySchema` (base64url, 43 to 128 characters) and `devicePlatformRequestSchema`'s optional `redemptionKey`. Sent with the first redemption by the platform service alone, it lets the same proof and the same key be redeemed again within the claim's ten minutes, each repetition revoking the platform credential the previous one issued. Without it, or with another key, a spent proof is the same 401 `invalid_grant`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.22.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **One SVG character renderer on web and native.** Saved character recipes, presets, live avatars and explicit portraits share packaged vector geometry, gaze and authored idle/reaction/work motion. Thirteen independently generated geometric body shapes and the definitive Gallery/Playground use the same catalog and editor. Visible agent avatars animate at every size; reduced motion, background and offscreen suspension remain respected.
- **Immediate avatar editing with history.** Undo, redo and reset preserve unrelated agent fields, drag changes form one history entry, and nearby shape preparation is bounded. Skin colors share a perceptual tone floor of 45 across saved recipes, palette, typed values and the visible picker.

### Fixed

- Eye placement follows the selected shape for presets and edited recipes. Eyewear keeps its original contours, attachments seat against the body, and interrupted work/reaction/idle changes preserve the displayed pose. Work text and hands leave with their panel. The retired bulb is no longer offered or restored from saved data.
- Shared frame scheduling and geometry caches avoid repeated work without merging independent interactions. Heavy projection reuses temporary coordinates while retaining immutable frames. Dense mixed-avatar performance remains limited; the measured development-browser and memory limits are documented without claiming mobile readiness.
- Sidebar edge fades follow the actual painted surface and viewport, retain rounded clipping, and stay behind the shared scrollbar. Short and narrow panes retain reachable footer content.

### Tests

- Canonical shape, eye and eyewear fitting, source immutability, transitions, cache lifetime, color policy and editor history have focused regression coverage. Browser runners cover actual pointer selection, consumer routing, crowds and sidebar scrolling. Before the publication artwork replacement, the projection optimization was compared across 1,530 frames, 170 eye-only views and 36 animated transitions without changing output; replacement shapes receive fresh geometry and attachment checks.

### Consumers

Bump to 17.22.0. Character and provider APIs remain source compatible, including `useAvatarRendererCapabilities`. Hosted runtime URLs, persistent raster still storage and the historical renderer choice are deprecated and inert: no WebGL/WebView or optional native GPU companion is selected. The offline authored geometry source remains a development extraction input. Native SVG drawing still requires device validation; browser results are not ARM or GPU-consumption guarantees.

entries.title: @oxy.so/contracts 6.21.0
entries.content:
A platform's credential from the QR approval (ADR 0058 R6, amended 2026-11-08).

### Added

- `platformSession.ts`: `devicePlatformRequestSchema` (`{ device: { deviceId, deviceSecret }, platformClient }`, strict) and `DevicePlatformRequest`, the body of `POST /session/device/platform`. The answer is the password sign-in's `LoginResult`, its `deviceSecret` the platform credential.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.15.2
entries.content:
### Added

- **A platform's setup store is told how the sign-in happened.** `authStateStore.save(state, context)`: `context` is `SetupSignInContext`, `{ method: 'qr' | 'password' | 'emailCode' | 'signup', password? }`. `'qr'` is an approval from a device the person already holds (the QR, the Commons identity), passwordless, so OxyOS asks no password and its service redeems the approval for its credential (`POST /session/device/platform`, ADR 0058 R6). `'password'` carries the password just typed, after its second factor too, so the platform can reuse it once instead of asking again. Only a store the app provided receives the context; the platform's own stores never do. The SDK drops the password once the sign-in commits or fails, and never persists or logs it. `handleWebSession(session, setup?)` takes it; `PlatformSetupAuthStateStore`, `SetupSignInContext` and `SetupSignInMethod` are exported.

### Fixed

- **No route an account cannot use.** A change that needs "confirm it's you" (`ReauthStep`: set or change the password, the email, the authenticator, deleting the account) offered an account with neither an email nor a password a "current password" field for a password it does not have. It now offers neither and says the account needs an email first. An account without an email is never offered the email code (unchanged), and one with an email but no password is never asked for a password.

### Consumers

No API removed. OxyOS bumps.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.21.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **The person's backups** (`PlatformFiles.backups`, what a file manager's *Browse Versions…* and *Browse Backups* need, a Mac's Time Machine; OxyOS ADR 0059): `PlatformFileBackups`, optional as `tags` is, present on a platform that makes backups. `state()` says where they are kept (`PlatformBackupsState`: its `destinations`, `PlatformBackupDestination` a disk or a share, whether each is reachable, its newest and oldest backup; the `lastBackup`; whether one is `backingUp`) and `watch(listener)` hears it change; an application shows its backup commands only while a destination is named. `versions(uri)` lists an item's versions newest first (`PlatformFileVersion`: its `PlatformBackup`, size and time of change; a file once for each backup it changed in, a folder in every backup); `contents(backup, folderUri)` what a folder held then (`PlatformBackupItem`, each by its `uri` where it was); `restore(backup, uri, options)` writes it back as the person, where it is or was or into `to` (Restore to…), beside an item of the same name as Time Machine names it (`notes (original).txt`) unless `replace` is asked, with `onProgress` and an abortable `signal`, answering `PlatformRestored` (`uri`, and `skipped` items of a folder: links leading out of it, devices). Errors carry a `PlatformBackupError` `code` (the file errors, `unavailable`, `not-permitted`, `cancelled`). All from `@oxy.so/bloom/platform-surface`. `docs/platform-surface.mdx`.

### Tests

- `PlatformFiles.test.tsx`: the backups reach the application through its files and its own provider, absent where the platform makes none; a state, a version, a folder's contents and restores (Keep Both, Replace into another folder, progress) through typed fixtures, so `tsc` holds the shapes.

### Consumers

Bump to 17.21.0. Nothing changes for an application that does not read `backups`. An adapter whose platform makes backups gives `files.backups`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.15.1
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A setup client keeps no device once its session is over.** A platform's setup client (`authStateStore`, OxyOS's login screen) hands its credential to the platform and keeps none, so a lost token cannot be re-minted and the provider signs out. It now drops the device with the session (its state, directory and credential). Kept, the device directory went on listing the account just lost, and the sign-in offered it as "Choose an account" before the QR, a device picker on a screen that is not a device's and that could only start the same sign-in again (OxyOS, 2026-11-08). Apps with their own store are unchanged.

### Consumers

No API change. OxyOS bumps.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.20.3
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A settings rail's selection moving draws only the rows it moves between.** Every `RailRow` rendered at each page shown: the rail handed the rows the navigation's `selectPage`, which is made anew at every page, and with the platform's keyboard (a rail beside its page is one Tab stop) each row's roving props were new objects with new handlers and a new `ref` at every render. `RailRow` is memoized, the rail gives it one selection handler for as long as it lives, and `useNativeRovingGroup`'s `itemProps` now gives each option the same props object for as long as it is (or is not) the stop, its handlers and `ref` the same functions for as long as the group lives (so a host view's ref is no longer detached and attached again at each render, for every roving group: segmented controls, radio groups, tabs, category bars). With `groups` kept the same objects, showing another page draws two rows. OxyOS's Settings drew its 17 rows and their icons at every page shown.

### Tests

- `SettingsRailSelectionRenders.test.tsx` (native, with and without the platform's keyboard): moving the selection draws again exactly the two rows it moves between, and keeping it draws none. Red before the fix.

### Consumers

Bump to 17.20.3. Keep `groups` stable across renders (memoised) to have it.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.44.0
entries.content:
The Oxy Keychain's client (ADR 0063 step 2): the `/keychain` routes as `oxy.keychain`, and `KeychainClient`, one device's side of the vault, over the 7.43 cryptography. Shape and flows in docs/identity/keychain.md#sdk.

### Added

- **`oxy.keychain`**: `state`, `create`, `appendRoster`, `ownWrap`, `recoveryWrap`, `reset`, `enrollments.{create, list, get, postApproverNonce, reveal, approve, cancel}`, `items.{list, put, delete}`. No cryptography (the routes carry only ciphertext); answers checked with `@oxy.so/contracts/client`, never cached, writes never retried by the transport; refusals are `OxyApiError` with a `KEYCHAIN_ERROR_CODES` code. `openClient({ store })` loads the client from `@oxy.so/core/crypto` on first use.
- **`KeychainClient`** (`@oxy.so/core/crypto`), driven by the platform's `KeychainDeviceStore` (`load`/`save`/`clear` of a JSON-safe record whose secret fields the platform keeps in its secure storage): `status`, `createVault` + `confirmRecoveryKey` (the recovery key is shown once and must be typed back before Oxy sees the vault), `requestToJoin` / `revealWhenOpened` / `completeJoin` / `cancelJoin`, `listJoinRequests` / `openJoinRequest` / `joinRequestCode` / `approveJoinRequest(id, { codeConfirmed: true })` / `denyJoinRequest`, `joinWithRecoveryKey`, `sync` (and `sync({ full: true })`, which re-reads the whole vault and requires every item the device knows), `putItem` / `deleteItem` (on `409`: re-read, higher counter, last writer wins per item, the replaced version returned and a login's password kept in its history; a deleted id is never written again, so a write that met a deletion is kept under a new id, `deletedId`), `removeMember` and `sweepOrphans` (with a rotation), `replaceRecoveryKey`, `reset`, `forget`.
- Every answer is verified before anything is kept (roster from genesis against the pinned genesis and head, the vault summary, wraps and the generations held, items and their counters, enrollments, write answers). A failure throws **`KeychainIntegrityError`** (`reason`: `fork`, `rollback`, `genesis_mismatch`, `roster`, `summary`, `wrap`, `item`, `counter`, `incomplete`, `enrollment`, `answer`) and writes nothing. **`KeychainStateError`** (`reason`) when the device's state does not allow the operation; **`KeychainConflictError`** after four conflicting writes.

entries.title: @oxy.so/bloom 17.20.2
entries.content:
### Fixed

- **A sidebar tree's selection moving draws only the rows it moves between.** Every `TreeRow` was handed `selectedTreeItem`, so a selection moving drew every row of the tree again, with its icon, its `leading`, its `actions` and its drop target, though only two changed. A row now sees the selection only when it is the row or nests under it (and the rows above it, which pass it down): with a `tree` kept the same objects while what it shows is the same, going to another place draws two rows. Dropsea's sidebar drew 18 rows and their 350 components at every navigation; going back to a folder on OxyOS spent a fifth of its JavaScript there (OxyOS's `perf-dropsea-scaled`, step 19).

### Tests

- `SidebarTreeSelectionRenders.test.tsx` (native): moving the selection draws again exactly the two rows it moves between, a nested row draws only its branch and the row it leaves, and keeping it draws nothing. Red before the fix.

### Consumers

Bump to 17.20.2. Keep `tree` and `onTreeItemPress` stable across renders (memoised, or compiled by the React Compiler) to have it: a tree made anew at each render still draws every row.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.43.0
entries.content:
The Oxy Keychain's cryptography (ADR 0063 D8), under `@oxy.so/core/crypto`. Formats only: the `oxy.keychain` routes come with the server's contracts.

### Added

- **Seal** (`keychainSeal`, `keychainOpenSealed`): age's X25519 recipient construction, HKDF-SHA256 (salt `E ‖ R`, info `oxy.keychain.seal.v1`), XChaCha20-Poly1305 with AAD; an all-zero shared secret (a low-order key) is refused.
- **Keys**: `generateDeviceKeys`, `deviceKeysFromSecrets`, `exportPublicKeys`, `zeroizeKeyPairs`; the recovery key (`generateRecoveryKey`, `formatRecoveryKey`, `parseRecoveryKey`, `deriveRecoveryKeys`, `recoveryKeyMatches`).
- **Keyring and wraps**: `createKeyring`, `rotateKeyring`, `encodeKeyring`/`decodeKeyring` (JCS), `wrapAad`, `wrapSigningInput`, `createWrap`, `verifyWrap`, `openWrap`.
- **Roster**: entry builders (`genesisBody`, `addBody`, `removeBody`, `generationBody`, `recoveryBody`), `signRosterBody`, `rosterSigningInput`, `rosterEntryHash`, and `verifyRoster`, which verifies from genesis (pinned genesis hash, extension of the known head, signer membership at each point, the recovery key only where it may sign, `remove` and `recovery` each followed by `generation` (ADR 0063 D6 as amended here: a replaced recovery key opens nothing written after it), closed schemas) and returns the members, recovery keys and generation; `KeychainRosterError.reason` says why a roster was refused.
- **Enrollment**: `enrollmentCommitment`, `verifyEnrollmentCommitment`, `enrollmentComparisonCode` (six digits).
- **Items**: strict schemas for `login`, `passkey`, `totp`, `note`, `wifi` (`validateItem`), JCS padded with spaces to a multiple of 256, `encryptItem`/`decryptItem` under a keyring generation, `isItemCounterAcceptable`/`nextItemCounter`.
- **`generateStrongPassword`** (four groups of five from `[a-zA-Z0-9]`, every class, unbiased) and RFC 6238 TOTP (`totpCode`, `hotpCode`, `parseOtpauthUri`; SHA-1/256/512).
- `src/crypto/keychain/__tests__/vectors.json`: the cross-implementation test vectors the OxyOS keychain service reproduces (shape in docs/identity/keychain.md#test-vectors).
- Dependency: `@noble/curves` (catalog), for Ed25519 and X25519.

entries.title: @oxy.so/contracts 6.20.0
entries.content:

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.41.0
entries.content:
A backup the person deleted stays deleted (owner's decision, 2026-11-07): rotating a key never silently re-uploads the encrypted identity backup of a person who deleted theirs.

### Changed

- **`rotateKey` respects the deletion.** When `backup.status().optedOut` (read by `readBeforeRotation`, which now returns `optedOut`), the rotation uploads nothing and marks nothing owed, and the result carries `backupOptedOut: true`; the replaced key is still kept in this device's ring for spending, and off the phone only its own recovery phrase recovers it. `RotateKeyOptions.createBackup: true` is the person's explicit opt-in from the rotation flow: the re-seal then sends `optIn` and the backup is owed (with the choice) until sealed. A person with no backup on record (never made one, or deleted it before deletions were recorded) is re-sealed as before unless `createBackup: false` (they declined it when shown), which also uploads nothing and owes nothing (`backupOptedOut`); `readBeforeRotation` now also returns `superseded`. A person with a backup (current or superseded) is re-sealed as before whatever `createBackup` says.
- **`backup.create(phrase, { optIn })`.** Pass `optIn: true` only from a control the person pressed; over a deletion, an upload without it throws `IdentityBackupOptedOutError` (exported) and drops this device's owed entry.
- **`backup.isOwed()` never nags a person who deleted their backup**, on any device: an owed entry without the person's choice is checked against `status().optedOut` and dropped. **`backup.delete()`** clears this device's owed entry once Oxy confirmed the deletion.
- `BackupOwedEntry.optIn` and `markBackupOwed(userId, { optIn })`: the person's choice travels with the owed entry until the seal.

### For Peable

Nothing to change. Retired keys stay in the device ring whatever the backup; a person without a backup recovers a previous key on another phone only with that key's phrase (Commons, Backup & recovery → Previous keys).

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.40.0
entries.content:
Round-7 security review of the Peable mainnet identity receive: R7-2, R7-4 (core half), R7-5, R7-10, R7-11.

### Security

- **R7-2: a superseded backup's keys are kept before the swap, and it is replaced only with its acknowledgement.** `rotateKey` keeps every key the previous backup carries in the ring (bound when the key history names it, quarantined otherwise) BEFORE `POST /auth/rotate/complete`, and does not rotate when one cannot be kept. The previous backup's locator is kept in the owed entry and sent as `replacesLookupId` by the re-seal, and by a later `backup.create` when the re-seal failed. `backup.create(phrase, { previousPhrase })` opens a superseded backup with the previous phrase and carries its keys; `backup.restoreRetiredKeys(previousPhrase)` records the acknowledgement once every key of the account's superseded backup is bound in the ring. An unacknowledged upload throws `IdentityBackupSupersededError` (exported). `readBeforeRotation` returns `replacesLookupId`.
- **R7-4: a key that cannot be read now is never "not this key".** With the `publicKey` selector, `KeyManager.deriveScopedSeed` and `signSocialReceive` resolve `null` only when the key is DEFINITIVELY not held, and throw `IdentityUnavailableError` when it may be: a keychain or ring read that failed, a listed key whose private half cannot be read, and on Android outside Commons an identity host that did not answer, or that lists (or describes as current) the key without using it (settled with `listRetiredKeys` + `describe`). `listRetiredIdentityKeys` throws `RetiredKeyRingUnreadableError` when Commons' host did not answer, instead of reading as empty. `getRetiredPrivateKeyStrict` / `getOrganizationPrivateKeyStrict` are the strict readers (internal).
- **R7-5: a planted quarantine flood cannot stop re-validation or a rotation.** `MAX_QUARANTINED_RING_ENTRIES` (64) is per ring, with `MAX_QUARANTINED_RING_ENTRIES_TOTAL` (256) across rings. `quarantineRetiredIdentityKey(key, selector, { exempt: true })` is never refused by the bound: the rotation's held slot keys, organization re-validation and keys a phrase-opened backup carried use it. Quarantined entries whose private half is gone are dropped before a refusal. `revalidateHeldOrganizationKeys` no longer throws: an organization that fails stays pending and the others proceed.
- **R7-10: one owed-backup entry per account.** `markBackupOwed(userId, { supersededLookupId? })`, `clearBackupOwed(userId?)` (without an id: every entry), `backupOwedEntry(userId)`, `restoreBackupOwed(userId, entry)`; the pre-7.40 value (a bare account id) reads as its account's entry. A refused rotation puts back what was owed before it instead of clearing. `isOwed` and the seal read and clear only the signed-in account's entry. `backupOwedFor()` answers any one owed account.
- **R7-11: planted organization ids cost no network read.** Re-validation settles ids with no held pair (and malformed ids) locally in one write (`settleOrganizationRevalidations`), then asks Oxy about at most `MAX_REVALIDATIONS_PER_LAUNCH` (16) organizations per launch.

### For Peable

Treat `IdentityUnavailableError` (`error.name === 'IdentityUnavailableError'`) from `deriveScopedSeed` / `signSocialReceive` with `{ publicKey }`, and a throw from `listRetiredIdentityKeys`, as "cannot tell now": keep the payment's key as possibly held, show the wallet as locked or Commons as unavailable, retry later. Only `null` (or a list that answered) means the key is not on this device.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.39.0
entries.content:
Round-6 security review of the Peable mainnet identity receive: R6-3, R6-5, R6-8, R6-9, R6-10, R6-12, R6-14 and the dev-build note.

### Security

- **A v1 migration record is not the end (R6-3).** The access-group completion record carries its sweep version (`v: 2`). Core 7.32 (Commons 1.8, 1.9) wrote `v: 1` after adopting nothing on a device without the identity marker, or after adopting organization pairs nothing vouched for. A run that meets `v: 1` now sweeps the shared group as an unproven device does (every valid key and phrase kept QUARANTINED, read back, then deleted there) and lists every organization this device holds a pair for in the v2 record; only then is `v: 2` written. Commons calls `revalidateHeldOrganizationKeys(read)` at launch: a held pair equal to the key the organization publishes stays; any other is kept quarantined in that organization's ring, read back, and removed as the live pair (index entry and Android mirror too), to be bound by `claimRetiredOrganizationKeys` only if the organization's history names it. An organization whose key cannot be read now stays pending.
- **Pre-history keys can be proven (R6-5).** `oxy.identity.claimQuarantinedKeys(history?)` asks Oxy (`POST /identity/key-history/claim`) to add to the signed-in account's key history each QUARANTINED personal key this device holds that the history does not name, with a possession signature made inside the ring (`signWithQuarantinedIdentityKey`; the private key never leaves it). Oxy adds a key only when its own records prove it was that account's root. At most 8 keys per call, each tried once per process. `listQuarantinedIdentityKeys()` lists them.
- **A backup a rotation kept is never restored as the identity (R6-8).** An envelope the API marks `superseded` (an older client rotated and could not re-seal) is refused by `backup.restore`, while `backup.restoreRetiredKeys` gives back its key and the keys it carried.
- **The owed backup is cleared only by a confirmed upload (R6-9).** `rotateKey` marks the backup owed only after every step that cannot change anything server-side, and clears it only on a definitive 4xx refusal of `/auth/rotate/complete`; an ambiguous failure (no response, a 5xx, a DID that cannot be read) keeps it. `backup.create` seals only under the account's CURRENT key (a stale phrase uploads nothing) and clears the flag only when the server answered the upload.
- **No key is bound to an account its history does not name (R6-10).** `rotateKey` reads the key history first (unreadable: nothing changes), refuses a key that is not the account's current root, and keeps any other key a slot holds bound only when the history names it, QUARANTINED otherwise (`quarantineRetiredIdentityKey`). Keys a backup carries are bound the same way on create, `restore` and `restoreRetiredKeys`; with no readable history they are all quarantined.
- **The ring never lives in the shared group (R6-12).** Ring items are read, written and deleted in the wallet group only (`groupedKeychainStore(..., { ownGroupOnly: true })`): the Peable wallet's pre-migration fallback no longer covers them.
- **Bounded work and ring growth (R6-14).** One migration run looks at most at `MAX_MIGRATION_ORGANIZATIONS` (100) organizations, the device's own index first. The ring holds at most `MAX_QUARANTINED_RING_ENTRIES` (64) quarantined entries; past that a new one is refused (`RetiredKeyQuarantineFullError`), the migration reports the unit `over-limit` and LEAVES the shared copy (never lost, never trusted) without keeping the run from settling, and a Commons write meeting such a copy leaves it too (`SharedCopyKeeper` resolves whether the copy may be deleted).
- **A dev Commons or dev wallet writes nothing into the production shared group.** Its `shared` items (the identity public key) are no-ops; it derives its public key from its own private key.

### Added

- `revalidateHeldOrganizationKeys`, `OrganizationPublishedKeyReader`, `quarantineRetiredIdentityKey`, `listQuarantinedIdentityKeys`, `signWithQuarantinedIdentityKey`, `MAX_QUARANTINED_RING_ENTRIES`, `RetiredKeyQuarantineFullError`; `oxy.identity.claimQuarantinedKeys`; the `over-limit` migration outcome; `GroupedKeychainStoreOptions`.

### Changed

- `SharedCopyKeeper` resolves a boolean (whether the shared copy may be deleted).

### Consumers

Commons 1.11.0 calls `revalidateHeldOrganizationKeys` before binding quarantined organization keys and `claimQuarantinedKeys` before binding its personal ring. The Peable wallet: nothing to change.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.14.0
entries.content:
### Security

- **The device-session slot never prompts (R6-16).** The iOS shared device-session credential (`oxy_device_session`) is read through `readSharedWithoutInteraction` (`@oxy.so/core` 7.38.0), never expo-secure-store's read, which also tries an `:auth` copy. Any Oxy app could plant one in the shared group and make every Oxy app show Face ID at cold boot.
- **A locked keychain is not an empty one (R6-13).** The iOS `OxyIdentity.readKeychainItemWithoutInteraction` THROWS when it meets `errSecInteractionNotAllowed` (or `errSecAuthFailed`) while protected data is unavailable (the device is locked), instead of answering "absent". An item that needs the user is still skipped (`nil`) while the device is unlocked. Commons' access-group migration therefore defers on a locked phone instead of settling with copies it could not see, and the device-session read reports `unavailable`. Native: an app needs a new build.

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.38.0
entries.content:
### Added

- `readSharedWithoutInteraction(store, key, options, { accessGroup })` is exported from `@oxy.so/core/session` (with the `KeychainStoreLike` type): read one item of the SHARED iOS keychain group without ever prompting the user (security review R6-16). Any Oxy app can plant an `:auth` copy (an item stored with `requireAuthentication`) in that group, and expo-secure-store's own read would answer it with a Face ID prompt; this reads only the `:no-auth` and legacy copies through `@oxy.so/services`' `OxyIdentity.readKeychainItemWithoutInteraction`, and through expo-secure-store on a native module that predates it. Use it for every read of the shared group.

An unlisted `Origin` (every non-browser MCP client, such as Grok) got no OAuth challenge and never reached login. - The iOS `OxyIdentity` native module answers `readKeychainItemWithoutInteraction(key, service, accessGroup)`: one expo-secure-store item read with an `LAContext` that refuses interaction, from its `:no-auth` and legacy copies only, never the `:auth` copy that would show a Face ID prompt (round-5 review R5-9). `@oxy.so/core` 7.36.0 reads the shared keychain group through it. Native: an app needs a new build to get it; until then it reads through expo-secure-store as before.

### Changed

entries.title: @oxy.so/core 7.36.0
entries.content:
Round-5 security review of the Peable mainnet identity receive: R5-3, R5-5, R5-6, R5-7, R5-9 and the R4-12 remainder.

### Security

- **Nothing in the shared keychain group is lost (R5-3).** With no identity marker, the iOS access-group migration still adopts nothing, but it no longer leaves the shared copies behind: every valid key and phrase there (the personal slots, the shared slot, the personal phrase, every organization pair and phrase either index names) is kept in the retired ring QUARANTINED, read back, and only then deleted. A Commons secret write or delete that finds a different copy of the item in the shared group keeps it the same way first (`setSharedCopyKeeper`), and fails without writing when it cannot; a copy equal to the value written is simply deleted.
- **Development builds never touch the shared group (R5-5).** With `variant: '.dev'` the migration reads, moves and deletes nothing there (it only writes its own completion record), the read and delete plans of identity secrets and spending keys exclude it, and a write never deletes a copy there.
- **The encrypted backup never drops a key (R5-6).** `oxy.identity.backup.create(phrase)` first opens the backup that phrase already has (404: none; any other failure throws and nothing is uploaded), keeps its carried retired keys in the ring (owner: the signed-in account) and in the new payload, reads the ring strictly (`holdsRetiredRing()` tells "no ring in this app" from "a ring that cannot be read"), and refuses to seal when a key the previous backup carried would be missing. `rotateKey` reads the current backup with the current phrase BEFORE the server swap (which deletes it) and carries its retired keys and its key into the backup sealed under the new phrase; a backup that exists but cannot be read (no phrase on the device, or a failure other than 404) stops the rotation with nothing changed. On web the backup is re-sealed after a rotation when the account had one.
- **Organization keys are adopted only on the device's own word (R5-7).** The migration adopts a shared organization pair only when it equals the pair this device already keeps for that organization in the wallet group; anything else is kept quarantined in the organization's ring, and the live index gains only organizations this device holds. Commons binds quarantined organization entries with `claimRetiredOrganizationKeys(accountId, publicKeys)` against the organization's key history (`oxy.accounts.identityKey.get`) and makes the current one the live pair again with `adoptOrganizationKeyFromRing(accountId, currentPublicKey)`.
- **No slot write in a rotation drops a key (R4-12).** Before `rotateKey` overwrites the personal slots, every key they hold that is neither the key being replaced nor the new one (`KeyManager.heldIdentityPrivateKeys()`) is kept in the ring; when that cannot be confirmed nothing is overwritten (`localPersistFailed`).
- **R5-9.** The shared group is read without user interaction (the `OxyIdentity` native read of `@oxy.so/services` 14.13.0, `@oxy.so/protocol` 1.11.0), so an item another app planted there with `requireAuthentication` cannot stall Commons behind Face ID prompts; an older native module reads as before. A failed (`incomplete`) migration opens the shared-group fallback only for the proven items that could not move, per (service, key), and `ensureKeychainGroupsMigrated` retries it on a later access (30 s, doubling, five times per process) as well as on the next launch. The organization index is read strictly (`OrganizationKeyIndexUnreadableError`): never overwritten, surfaced by `listOrganizationKeys`, `storeOrganizationKey` and `deleteOrganizationKey`. The backup envelope is version 2 and the API refuses (409) an upload of a lower version than the stored one. A rotation marks the backup OWED before the swap and `backup.create` clears it once sealed: `oxy.identity.backup.isOwed()`.

### Added

- `holdsRetiredRing`, `claimRetiredOrganizationKeys`, `listQuarantinedOrganizationKeys`, `adoptOrganizationKeyFromRing`, `OrganizationKeyIndexUnreadableError`; `oxy.identity.backup.isOwed()`; `KeyManager.heldIdentityPrivateKeys`, `markBackupOwed`, `clearBackupOwed`, `backupOwedFor`; `readSharedWithoutInteraction` and the `name` argument of `keychainReadPlan`.

### Changed

- `setHolderSharedSecretFallback` takes the item names to open (empty closes it) instead of a boolean.

### Consumers

The Peable wallet: nothing to change for the wallet's own reads; organization keys of an upgraded phone reappear once Commons 1.10.0 has bound them. Commons 1.10.0 binds quarantined organization keys at launch, shows the owed-backup banner, and keeps its own flags out of the shared group.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.11.0
entries.content:
### Added

- **Host mode (ADR 0058 decision 1).** When a platform has registered a session host (`@oxy.so/core/host`) before the app runs, `OxyProvider` with `sessionMode: 'account'` takes its session from it: the host's token through `setAccessTokenProvider` and the refresh handler (`preflight`, `response-401`), the account from its snapshot, a revision change as one transition (token dropped and epoch bumped, the new account's token awaited, then the account published), offline signed in with no token. Nothing is persisted and there is no cold boot, OAuth return lane, identity pin, `SessionClient`, device directory, switcher, bridge, background credential or `/session/device/*` call. `useAuth().signIn()`, `openAccountDialog()`, a switch and `logout()` call `host.request(...)` only (`logout()` resolves `{ status: 'requested' }`); the user socket authenticates with the app token. A host with an unknown contract runs the app signed out. `'identity'` is never hosted. App assertions are not attempted in host mode until the server's `oxyos`/`astro` assertion lane exists.
- **`OxyProvider authStateStore`**, the seam for a platform's setup client (OxyOS's login screen): every credential write goes through the given store and nowhere else (no platform store, no shared device slot, no background credential). A registered host wins over it.
- `HostedSessionError`, thrown by what a hosted provider leaves to the platform (`handleWebSession`, `getDeviceSessions`, `updateDeviceName`, `switchSession`).
- `LogoutResult` gains `{ status: 'requested' }` (host mode only).

### Changed

- Needs `@oxy.so/core` `^7.34.0`.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.10.0
entries.content:
### Security

- iOS: the session store is this app's own (ADR 0062 D6 of the oxy repo). `oxy.auth.v1`, the warm token, the sign-out marker and the identity pin go to the app's own keychain group (`<TEAM>.<bundle id>`) and are never read from or deleted in the shared group, where every app but Commons and the Peable wallet used to share one copy; the sign-out marker is still honoured there, since it can only withhold. Cross-app sign-on stays the device-session slot.

### Added

- The iOS `OxyIdentity` native module answers `keychainApplicationAccessGroup(prefix)`: writes a probe item into `<prefix><bundle id>` explicitly and returns that group, or `nil` when the keychain refuses it. Native: an app needs a new build to get it; until then it keeps the placement it had.

entries.content:

Every answer must echo the key (and the account) asked for, so a Commons that predates them answers `null`, never the current key. A list with one malformed entry is refused whole.

entries.title: @oxy.so/services 14.8.0
entries.content:
### Security

- iOS keychain access-group split (ADR 0062 of the oxy repo, docs/identity/ios-keychain-access-groups.md). The device-session credential is written to and read from the shared group with the real, team-prefixed `accessGroup` (`keychainAccessGroup` was never an `expo-secure-store` option); Commons' default group is now the identity group, so without it Commons would write the credential where no sibling reads it. An app's own SecureStore items in Commons and the Peable wallet go to their default group explicitly and are read from it first, so a pre-split copy never shadows a newer one; every other app's calls are unchanged. The ambient `expo-secure-store` shim is gone.

### Added

- The iOS `OxyIdentity` native module answers `keychainDefaultAccessGroup()`: the access group a probe item written without a group lands in (the first `keychain-access-groups` entry, team prefix included), which `@oxy.so/core` reads the app's role and the prefix from. Native: an app needs a new build to get it; until then it behaves as before.

### Changed

- Needs `@oxy.so/core` `^7.29.0`.
